Customer is interested in a pilot on their VPC; security and dedicated capacity questions remain. Agreed to share detailed compatibility matrix and run a short benchmark pilot.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted vs private deployment tradeoffs
Security controls: SOC2, KMS, RBAC, audit logs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Chen (Emerald Clinic CMO), Allen Park (CTO), Riley Torres (Data Engineer)

Auto-summary: quick model catalog walkthrough, runbook for pilot, share security and compat artifacts.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account, with me is sofia our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Dr. Maya Chen: good thanks, appreciate you fitting this in. we sent over a quick agenda - want to see the model catalog and what you recommend for clinical note summarization and triage.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: perfect, that's exactly what we'll focus on. sofia is going to walk through the catalog, benchmarking data, and the compatibility matrix — and then we'll talk pilot next steps.
[00:35] Sofia Patel: hey all, quick note: i'll be referring to some reported benchmarks we ran on common hardware, there might be slight transription errors in the spreadsheet names but i'll share the sheet after. ok starting slide one, model catalog overview — we curate open models and surface performance profiles (latency, throughput, memory).
[01:05] Allen Park: quick qual question — currently we run on AWS EKS with some GPU workers (g5 and p4 tests). we also have strict data residency and require VPC connections for PHI.
[01:18] Sofia Patel: totally, we support private deployments and VPC peering for pilot. Dedicated pools can be reserved as well. for PHI we typically recommend private control plane with customer-managed networking and KMS integrations.
[01:39] Riley Torres: on the POC side we'd like to keep data in our VPC, and we'd want to run a small benchmark with our prompts and target 200ms avg latency for short summaries if possible.
[01:51] Sofia Patel: good to know. for 200ms you're likely looking at a smaller model family or aggressive quantization on larger models. our catalog highlights candidates by inference cost and latency.
[02:15] Jordan Lee: i'll pause there — high level, two routes: hosted (fast to start, pay-as-you-go) or dedicated/private (SLA, VPC, lower unit cost at scale). both support same API surface.
[02:35] Dr. Maya Chen: whats the delta on accuracy and hallucination risk across open models? we want medically-safe outputs.
[02:48] Sofia Patel: great question. accuracy varies with model size and instruction tuning; for clinical summarization we commonly recommend Mistral-7B-instruct and Llama-3-13B-instruct as starting points for a balance of latency and quality. for highest fidelity, Llama-3-70B or fine-tuned variants are better but cost/latency jump. we also run quality monitors and regression evals tied to your prompt set.
[03:20] [03:20] Allen Park: are those supported on dedicated GPUs? like can we run Llama-3-70B on p4 or do we need multi-node or quantization?
[03:33] Sofia Patel: 70B typically needs either multi-node or int8/4 quantization to fit on single p4. our compatibility matrix shows recommended hardware: sequence length, kv cache needs, and quantization profile. i'll attach that. sometimes we fallback to a 13B quantized profile for latency SLOs.
[04:05] Riley Torres: can you explain the kv cache and continuous batching stuff? how does that affect latency for chatty workloads?
[04:17] Sofia Patel: sure — continuous batching groups concurrent tokens for throughput, but we also have prefix/KV caching so repeated context doesn't re-compute. for chatty/short requests we use adaptive scheduling to prioritize latency SLOs, so batching is smaller. the cache helps with re-used prompts or templates.
[04:50] Jordan Lee: to ground this, let's look at a couple of concrete benchmarks we ran on open models — note these are representative:
[05:00] Sofia Patel: benchmark table (shared): Mistral-7B-instruct on A10G: 1.2x cost baseline, median p95 latency ~120ms for 128 token responses with batching 8; Llama-3-13B-instruct on p4: p95 ~220ms unquantized, int8 ~140ms; Llama-3-70B on multi-node unquantized p95 ~900ms, with quantization int8 ~320ms — numbers approximate and depend on seq len.
[05:45] Dr. Maya Chen: those look promising. what's the cost-per-1k tokens delta between 7B vs 13B on dedicated?
[05:56] Sofia Patel: rough numbers: Mistral-7B about $0.30 per 1k tokens on dedicated optimized runtime; Llama-3-13B about $0.65 unquantized, int8 brings to ~$0.38. 70B is >$2.5 unquantized, down to ~$0.9 with aggressive int4-like quant profiles. again these are example unit economics.
[06:30] [06:30] Allen Park: we need a compatibility matrix that maps your models to hardware (A10G, A100, p4), quantization support, and memory footprint.
[06:42] Sofia Patel: absolutely — that's in the doc. columns include model, recommended hw, quantization profile (int8, int4 experimental), max context/seq len expected, typical kv cache size, and known issues like kernel mismatches on older CUDA.
[07:08] Jordan Lee: competitor note — you mentioned Anthropic earlier. do you evaluate closed models?
[07:16] Sofia Patel: we surface performance for open models mostly; we do also show tradeoffs vs managed closed models (cost, SLOs, latency). customers sometimes choose hybrid: hosted for dev + dedicated for prod.
[07:35] Riley Torres: what's the rollout story — can we do canary and A/B for model variants?
[07:43] Sofia Patel: yes, the Console supports rollouts: canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies. you can pin model versions per route and measure token-level cost and latency in the Console.
[08:02] Dr. Maya Chen: security and compliance — we need SOC2, ISO, audit logs, SSO.
[08:11] Jordan Lee: we have those controls and we'll share the security pack. for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and support SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC. audit logs are available for all major actions.
[08:36] Allen Park: latency-wise, for local in-VPC inference, is it possible to achieve <200ms for short summaries with L3-13?
[08:47] Sofia Patel: yes with optimized kernels, int8, and pinned occupancy you can hit ~140-220ms depending on seq len and batch size. if you need consistent p95 <200ms, we'd recommend scoped pilot to validate with your prompts.
[09:12] [09:12] Jordan Lee: quick pivot to model selection guidance: we usually start with 2 model candidates — one smaller low-latency model as default (Mistral-7B) and one higher-quality fallback (Llama-3-13B). we can also surface tuned variants if you want domain adapted models.
[09:40] Dr. Maya Chen: do you offer fine-tuning or instruction-tuning as part of the pilot?
[09:47] Sofia Patel: we offer model hosting of fine-tuned artifacts and can facilitate fine-tuning workflows with your dataset but for PHI we'd recommend doing fine-tuning in your private environment or with a private deployment. we also do eval-based quality monitoring to detect regressions.
[10:10] Riley Torres: what's the turnaround for setting up a dedicated pilot in our VPC?
[10:19] Jordan Lee: typical timeline is 1-2 weeks for initial access (network, creds) + a week to run benchmarks and iterate. i'll put specific timeline in follow-up notes.
[10:35] Allen Park: licensing/cost model questions — is there committed pricing for Dedicated?
[10:41] Jordan Lee: yes, Dedicated has reserved capacity and commit tiers; we can show monthly/annual numbers. for pilots usually start hosted or small reserved capacity.
[11:00] Sofia Patel: showing a compatibility matrix excerpt now — (transcription) \"model catelog matrix\" — forgive the typo — Key rows: Mistral-7B, Llama-3-13B, Mistral-7B-FT (fine tuned), Llama-3-70B. columns: recommended GPUs, quantization support, notes on chunking for long contexts.
[11:40] Dr. Maya Chen: do you have any clinical customers who've done a pilot like ours? any case studies?
[11:47] Jordan Lee: yes, a regional clinic ran summarization + triage pilot; they used a 7B primary model with a 13B fallback for complex cases and saw 40% token cost savings after caching and batching optimizations. we'd be happy to share a redacted case study.
[12:05] Riley Torres: on the benchmarking scripts — can we run them in our EKS cluster or do you want to run from Redwood side?
[12:13] Sofia Patel: we can do both. for closed network we'd ask for a runner or temporary VPC peering; we can also provide a containerized benchmark harness you can run. it records latency distribution, token costs, and trace logs.
[12:35] [12:35] Allen Park: a few technical deep dive Qs: what about kernel selection and CUDA versions? we've had issues with older runtimes.
[12:44] Sofia Patel: compatibility matrix flags known kernel mismatches. runtime picks optimized kernels at start; we recommend CUDA 11.8+ for best perf on p4 & A100. we'll include kernel notes per model.
[13:05] Jordan Lee: some minor transcription noise here, but moving to a demo of the Console — sofia will share screen.
[13:13] Sofia Patel: (screen share) Console > Model Catalog. top filters: model family, seq len, recommended hardware, verified benchmarks. you can click a model to see full perf profile and a \"compatibility\" tab.
[13:45] [13:45] Sofia Patel: demo note: the \"compatibility\" tab lists tested GPUs, quantization compatibility, and expected peak memory for a given context size. you can also download the csv matrix.
[14:10] Dr. Maya Chen: can we export the config to terraform or infra as code?
[14:16] Sofia Patel: yes we have config templates and infra snippets for both Dedicated and Private deployments. we'll share those.
[14:30] Allen Park: what observability do you provide for model quality?
[14:35] Sofia Patel: Redwood Console provides per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdowns, trace hooks, and quality monitoring where you can tie eval sets to alerts. we can create regression alerts if a model's accuracy drops vs a reference set.
[14:56] [14:56] Riley Torres: about KV cache — if we have patient templates that repeat, the cache should reduce cost?
[15:04] Sofia Patel: exactly. prefix caching avoids re-encoding static templates and reduces compute per request. good for templated triage flows.
[15:20] Dr. Maya Chen: a concern — hallucination risk in discharge summaries is high. how do you recommend mitigation?
[15:30] Sofia Patel: approaches: instruction tuning with your prompts, retrieval-augmented generation to ground outputs, post-processing rules, and a human in the loop for final edits. we can help set up evals to flag hallucination risk.
[15:55] [15:55] Jordan Lee: quick pause — any blockers for a pilot from your perspective?
[16:03] Allen Park: main blockers: security approval, network setup for VPC peering, and confirming cost estimate.
[16:10] Jordan Lee: understood. we'll share the security pack and a dedicated cost estimate.
[16:22] Sofia Patel: demo note: switching to the Optimize surface — Optimize suggests batching/quantization settings per route and estimates unit cost savings. it also highlights models where int8 quantization is stable vs experimental int4.
[16:45] Dr. Maya Chen: will Optimize recommend model selection automatically based on our prompt set?
[16:51] Sofia Patel: yes — you can upload a representative prompt set and Optimize will score models by latency, cost, and a quality proxy from evals. it'll output a suggested default model and fallback rules.
[17:10] Riley Torres: that's helpful — we do have a canonical prompt set we can share.
[17:16] Sofia Patel: perfect — please include target KPIs in the upload so Optimize ranks by your constraints.
[17:28] [17:28] Allen Park: about private deployments: do we get the same console features when running Private?
[17:35] Sofia Patel: yes, Private includes the Console and telemetry; the control plane can be configured for customer-managed networking. RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration supported. some advanced optimizations require kernel-level runtime in the private package but we can ship that.
[17:58] Dr. Maya Chen: is there any special handling for PHI logs? retention, masking?
[18:06] Sofia Patel: we support configurable retention and token-level masking; also an option to route logs to your own S3/secure storage so Redwood doesn't store PHI if you prefer.
[18:28] Jordan Lee: stepping back to the catalog: any models you want us to highlight for the pilot?
[18:34] Dr. Maya Chen: probably start Mistral-7B plus Llama-3-13B fallback. if pilot looks good we may test a larger model later.
[18:44] Sofia Patel: sounds great. recommended quant profiles: Mistral-7B unquantized for dev; for production int8 gives good savings. Llama-3-13B int8 recommended for latency; we can test int4 experimentally in a controlled pilot.
[19:05] [19:05] Riley Torres: will the benchmark harness capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost?
[19:10] Sofia Patel: yes, it captures p50/p95/p99, token counts, and runtime traces for each request.
[19:25] Allen Park: scheduling: can we aim for network setup next week and run benchmarks the following week?
[19:33] Jordan Lee: yes we'll aim to start network setup by 2026-12-24 and benchmarks 12/29 - 01/05. i'll put exact dates in follow-up.
[19:46] [19:46] Sofia Patel: demo — switching to the model profile for Llama-3-13B: shows memory usage curve vs seq len, recommended batch sizes, and known issues — e.g., some older CUDA drivers show slowdowns due to kernel fallback.
[20:12] Dr. Maya Chen: one more compliance Q — if we use Private on-prem, is there support for HSM?
[20:20] Sofia Patel: yes Private supports HSM integrations and can be configured to use your KMS/HSM for key management.
[20:35] Jordan Lee: moving to wrap up — recap and next steps.
[20:40] Jordan Lee: recap: we'll share the model catalog CSV, compatibility matrix, security pack, and pricing. you'll share prompt set and grant VPC access for the pilot. agreed?
[20:53] Dr. Maya Chen: yes that's right.
[21:00] Allen Park: please include the cost delta for committed vs on-demand Dedicated.
[21:05] Jordan Lee: will do.
[21:12] Sofia Patel: final note — we'll include recommended quantization profiles and a sample terraform template to provision a pilot node.
[21:25] [21:25] Riley Torres: thanks, this was useful.
[21:30] Jordan Lee: thank you all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[21:35] (meeting moves to off-topic scheduling and minor clarifications)
[56:10] Jordan Lee: final quick note — action items are in the follow-up email, i'll list owners and dates. thanks everyone.
[56:25] Dr. Maya Chen: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — occasional mis-typed product names (\"catelog\"), and a few numeric approximations in benchmarks.
